quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report (filed 08-14-2026, consolidated, K-IFRS, reviewed by Samjong KPMG): H1 2026 revenue KRW 305,372,914M vs KRW 153,706,820M in H1 2025 (+98.7% YoY); gross profit KRW 201,213,884M (65.9% GM vs 34.9%); operating profit KRW 146,725,209M (48.0% margin) vs KRW 11,361,329M (12.9x); net profit KRW 118,849,733M (attributable KRW 118,370,658M) vs KRW 13,339,313M; basic EPS KRW 17,950 vs 1,929. Q2 2026 alone (04-01-2026 to 06-30-2026): revenue KRW 171,499,470M (+28.1% QoQ vs Q1 KRW 133,873,444M, +130.0% YoY vs KRW 74,566,317M), operating profit KRW 89,492,412M (52.2% margin, +56.4% QoQ vs KRW 57,232,797M, 19.1x YoY vs KRW 4,676,057M), net profit KRW 71,624,461M, EPS KRW 10,849. SEGMENTS H1: DS (memory, System LSI, foundry) revenue KRW 209,231,714M (+294.7% YoY, 68.5% of sales) and operating profit KRW 142,859,293M (97.4% of group OP; Q2 DS OP KRW 89,196,019M on Q2 DS revenue KRW 127,516,071M = 69.9% margin); DX (set) revenue KRW 100,677,119M (+5.7%) with OP KRW 2,148,877M (Q2 DX OP a KRW 818,805M LOSS as memory input costs rose); SDC revenue KRW 14,178,522M (+15.8%) OP KRW 1,043,353M; Harman revenue KRW 8,394,100M (+15.8%) OP KRW 636,826M. Memory product revenue KRW 195,620,223M in H1 (Q2 KRW 120,840,243M vs KRW 21,178,497M a year earlier, 5.7x) vs smartphones KRW 69,798,593M and TV/monitor KRW 15,445,566M. Memory ASP up ~220% vs the 2025 annual average; DRAM value share 39.4% (DRAMeXchange, company estimate) vs 34.0% in 2025. GEOGRAPHY (separate-entity domestic/export): China KRW 88,600.4B, Americas KRW 70,646.6B, Asia/Africa KRW 64,622.4B, Europe KRW 21,797.3B, Korea KRW 12,884.2B. Balance sheet 06-30-2026: cash KRW 92,916,382M plus short-term financial instruments KRW 97,036,646M; trade receivables KRW 96,408,968M (up from KRW 51,127,642M at 12-31-2025); inventories KRW 71,389,118M (DS KRW 38,056,737M); total borrowings ~KRW 22.4T; contract liabilities (customer prepayments) KRW 23,592,176M vs KRW 13,978,566M at year-end; debt-to-equity 31.1%. Operating cash flow H1 KRW 145,355,192M (vs 33,941,002M); capex (PP&E purchases) KRW 31,234,818M; treasury-share buybacks KRW 13,248,625M; dividends paid KRW 6,222,802M. R&D KRW 27,362,722M in H1 (9.0% of sales). S&P raised the outlook on its AA- rating to Positive in July 2026 (Moody's Aa2 Stable).

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report (08-14-2026), memory demand and order book: Q2 2026 memory demand was led by AI applications, and as Agentic AI spread the major hyperscaler customers kept submitting ADDITIONAL supply requests for AI-driven memory. In H2 the company expects hyperscaler infrastructure investment for AI market share and the acceleration of Agentic AI to keep demand strong for general-purpose computing servers as well as AI servers; mobile/PC demand is slowing on set-price increases, but incremental server DRAM/SSD and HBM demand will more than offset this, so the filing states the supply-demand GAP WILL WIDEN THROUGH NEXT YEAR (2027). In Q2, within the given production capacity, sales were focused on server applications with strong demand momentum: both DRAM and NAND achieved RECORD BIT SHIPMENTS and the server share of bit shipments hit an all-time high; HBM4 supply was expanded and the company was first in the industry to ship HBM4E samples to key customers. H2 outlook: despite production-increase efforts, demand growth is expected to exceed supply, so product mix will be optimised while continuously sensing demand changes. Overseas subsidiaries hold multi-year memory supply agreements with multiple global customers (terms confidential; total order value and delivery periods may change with customer demand and business progress) - disclosed as a supply-contract commitment in note 13 to the consolidated statements. Contract liabilities (customer prepayments etc.) rose to KRW 23,592,176M at 06-30-2026 from KRW 13,978,566M at 12-31-2025. Major customers in H1 2026 (alphabetical): Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Hong Kong Techtronics, Supreme Electronics; the top-5 customers were ~25% of total revenue. Separate-entity related-party sales through the semiconductor sales subsidiaries were KRW 103,194,471M via Samsung Semiconductor Inc. (US) and KRW 51,004,013M via Shanghai Samsung Semiconductor (China) in H1 2026 (SSI standalone Q2 revenue KRW 63,318,020M vs KRW 11,547,062M a year earlier, 5.5x).
quarterly_data.figure: Record DRAM and NAND bit shipments in Q2, server bit share all-time high; hyperscalers requesting additional AI memory supply; supply-demand gap to widen through 2027; multi-year memory LTAs with multiple global customers; top-5 customers ~25% of sales (Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, HK Techtronics, Supreme Electronics); contract liabilities KRW 23.6T (+69% YTD)

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report (08-14-2026), capacity, utilisation and capex: DS memory production capacity 1,318,144,864 thousand 1Gb-equivalent units in H1 2026 (package-out basis; FY2025 2,245,908,090 thousand), production 1,318,145 million 1Gb-equivalent units produced at Hwaseong and Pyeongtaek (Korea) and Xian (China); memory lines run 24 hours/3 shifts on 181 operating days and posted 100.0% UTILISATION (43,440 possible hours vs 43,440 actual). DS wafer purchase price fell ~10% vs the 2025 annual average (wafers KRW 1,150.0B of DS purchases, from Siltronic and SK Siltron; chemicals KRW 1,697.5B from Soulbrain and Dongwoo Fine-Chem). CAPEX: H1 2026 facility investment KRW 27,986.4B in total (DS KRW 25,603.0B, SDC KRW 1,334.6B, other KRW 1,048.8B), centred on advanced-process expansion/conversion and infrastructure at DS and SDC; the filing says investment continues to strengthen next-generation memory technology competitiveness and prepare for mid-to-long-term demand, while system semiconductors are investing to secure advanced-node capacity, with a focus on investment efficiency. PP&E carrying value KRW 224,371,952M at 06-30-2026 (+KRW 9,067.2B YTD; construction-in-progress KRW 60,237.3B); PP&E additions KRW 28,724.8B in H1 vs depreciation KRW 23,593.4B. Purchase commitments for PP&E/intangibles not yet incurred: KRW 30,543,192M (consolidated). Management Committee approved memory investment resolutions on 02-11-2026, 03-17-2026, 04-14-2026 (plus a GPU investment), 04-17-2026, 04-29-2026, 04-30-2026 and 05-15-2026 (two memory items plus a Foundry investment), a further Foundry investment on 05-28-2026 and overseas equity investments on 05-28-2026 and 06-05-2026; the board approved a capital contribution to the National AI Computing Center consortium on 04-30-2026. New subsidiaries in H1: Samsung Semiconductor Asia Holdings (Singapore) and Samsung Vietnam Semiconductor (SVS, semiconductor production, established 03-2026 in Thai Nguyen, Vietnam). US subsidiary Samsung Austin Semiconductor (SAS) had total assets KRW 36,260,678M at 06-30-2026; a USD 6,435,000K parent guarantee to the US Government covers SAS's CHIPS subsidy claw-back obligation (signed 12-20-2024). DX memory input prices rose ~211% vs the 2025 average and mobile AP prices ~6%.
quarterly_data.figure: Memory utilisation 100.0%; H1 memory output 1,318,145M 1Gb-eq units; H1 capex KRW 28.0T (DS KRW 25.6T); PP&E KRW 224.4T (CIP KRW 60.2T); capex commitments KRW 30.5T; 7 memory-investment resolutions Feb-May 2026; new Vietnam semiconductor subsidiary (SVS)

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report (08-14-2026), product and R&D pipeline (DS): HBM4 - world-first mass-production shipment (02-2026) of the industry's highest-performance HBM4 built on the most advanced 1c DRAM (10nm-class 6th generation) with a 4nm base die, running at 11.7 Gbps (up to 13 Gbps) against the 8 Gbps JEDEC standard, offered in 24GB (8-high) to 48GB (16-high) capacities, positioned as a logic-memory-foundry-packaging 'one-stop solution' with pre-emptive infrastructure investment for supply stability. HBM4E - industry-first 12-high HBM4E samples shipped 05-2026 at 14 Gbps per pin (up to 16 Gbps), 3.6 TB/s per stack (20%+ above HBM4), 16% better energy efficiency and 14% better thermal resistance than HBM4. Server DRAM: 1c (10nm-class 6th gen) DRAM in mass production since 06-2025 with 30%+ productivity and ~10% power gains, HBM included in the 1c line-up; SOCAMM2 LPDDR server module developed 12-2025 (2x RDIMM bandwidth, 55%+ lower power). Storage: PCIe 6.0 server SSD PM1763 developed (9th-gen V-NAND plus 4nm controller, 16TB, optimised for direct-to-chip liquid cooling); industry-first on-device-AI UFS 5.0 developed 06-2026 (10.8 GB/s, 2x UFS 4.1, 40% better power efficiency, up to 1TB); 24Gb GDDR7 in mass production since 01-2025 (42.5 Gbps, 1.92 TB/s). System LSI: Exynos Modem 5410, Exynos 1680, Exynos Connect 6375 launched; a new Custom SoC opportunity is being pursued for Agentic AI; the Power business is diversifying from mobile into SERVER power ICs; image sensors expanding into automotive. DX: Galaxy S26 series (03-2026), Galaxy Book6 (Intel Panther Lake, NVIDIA RTX 5060/5070 options), Micro RGB and Neo Mini LED TV lines; TV value share 30.6%, smartphone unit share 22.0% in H1 2026. Corporate: acquisition of ZF Friedrichshafen's ADAS business in progress (agreement signed 12-23-2025, closing expected in 2026); FlaktGroup (data-center central HVAC, acquired 11-06-2025) now consolidated with FlaktGroup Korea established in H1 2026; board approved a capital contribution to the National AI Computing Center consortium (04-30-2026); shareholder-return: KRW 5,346,072M of treasury shares (73,359,314 common, 13,603,461 preferred) cancelled 04-02-2026, KRW 13,248,625M of common shares bought back in H1 for employee stock compensation, quarterly dividend KRW 374/share for Q2; a 06-24-2026 exchange enquiry on a reported KRW 90T buyback was answered as 'under review, nothing decided' (re-disclosure due by 10-22-2026). Patents: 296,468 registered worldwide at 06-30-2026.
quarterly_data.figure: HBM4 mass production shipping since 02-2026 (11.7-13 Gbps, 1c DRAM + 4nm base die); HBM4E 12-high samples shipped 05-2026 (3.6 TB/s); PCIe 6.0 SSD PM1763 and UFS 5.0 developed; ZF ADAS acquisition closing 2026; KRW 5.3T shares cancelled 04-02-2026; KRW 90T buyback report 'under review'
